verdict.rationale: Gram's first-party platform MCP server lets an org admin do a long list of dashboard tasks without opening the dashboard: add MCP servers, manage plugins, skills, access roles, risk policies and telemetry, and read observability data. Its CLI also covers deployments and toolset installation. Neither surface is documented as full UI parity, and no public REST API or OpenAPI spec was found (the probe returned 404 on all candidate paths). Missing for 10: a documented general-purpose public API, an explicit claim of API/UI feature parity, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: An org admin working in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or another MCP client can find and add MCP servers, finish their setup, put them on a plugin, choose who receives a plugin, author skills, manage access roles, review shadow MCP servers, manage risk policies, configure telemetry delivery, and read observability data without opening the dashboard.
The gram CLI manages platform resources directly from the terminal.
